title: Inverse Standard Normal
summary: z from a central probability. FMLA 04/05 only go the other way. 156 bytes.

body.text: FMLA 04/05 map z → probability. This WebCal DSE-accurate inverse listing maps p = P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) → x using the exam table plus linear interpolation, so the digits match the HKEAA book. Prompt is p with 0 < p < 0.5. Table hits (two decimal z) print as a terminating two-decimal x. In-between values print the interpolated z; RCL A, B are the two table probabilities and RCL Y, M are the two z-grid points for the written working.

body.label: Memory / run mode
body.text: 156 bytes of the shared 680-byte pool. Create the slot in COMP. Type ? → : ◢ Goto Lbl If Then from SHIFT 3 (P-CMD).
Question: Use this program to solve the case: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3907.
Given: This p sits on the printed table, so x is exactly two decimals.
Question: Use this program to solve the case: P(0 ≤ Z ≤ x) = 0.3 (needs interpolation).
Given: After the run, RCL A ≈ 0.2995, RCL B ≈ 0.3023, RCL Y = 0.84, RCL M = 0.85.

items: Those four recalls are the interpolation lines you write in the script

body.text: Question: Use this program to solve the case: p outside (0, 0.5).
Given: Left tail, two-tail, or p ≥ 0.5 must be rewritten first.

items: P(Z ≤ a) = 0.9 → central slab is 0.4, then run 0.4; the printed x is a
P(Z ≥ a) = 0.1 is the same 0.4 slab
p = 0 or p ≥ 0.5 → Math ERROR or a stuck loop. Do not enter 0.5

body.label: Pitfalls
body.text: Fix 2, Fix 4, Norm 1 and Rnd( are the display-format commands — enter them from SET UP (SHIFT MODE) while editing. E is EXP, so E−4 is 10⁻⁴. e^( is SHIFT eˣ. p > 0.4973 can hit a multi-z table clash; AC then RCL M is the fallback. Source: WebCal standardnormal_6 program I.
